critical_code_review_comments: richieste.py::price_breakdown() correctly implements Spec 3 for IMPRESA: fee_client = round(jobby_fee/2, 2) and fee_provider = round(jobby_fee - fee_client, 2). Cents-safe: for odd cents jobby_fee (e.g., 8.11) client would pay 4.06 and provider 4.05, so JOBBY still receives the full amount.

For PERSONA_LF the same function overrides with fee_client=jobby_fee, fee_provider=0.0, provider_net=0.0 and total_client=lf_nominale+jobby_fee — semantics match spec (voucher nominale is separate from the fee, fee is paid IN ADDITION by the client).

confirm() writes pagamento_fee.importo=bd.get('fee_client', bd.get('jobby_fee', 0)) and pagamento_fee.jobby_fee_total=bd.get('jobby_fee', 0). This dual-field approach makes downstream accounting explicit: JOBBY collects jobby_fee_total total (half from client fee_client + half deducted from provider net).

pagamento_lavoro on impresa uses bd.get('provider_net', prop['price']) and records fee_provider=bd.get('fee_provider', 0). Fallback to prop['price'] handles legacy proposals without breakdown, but new flow always writes provider_net = work − fee_provider. Verified end-to-end.

list/[group].tsx onPress() prioritises the configurators map by cat_id before falling back to /businesses (proximity) or /request/<cat> (old flow). This ensures the 4 flagship services always land on the new configurators regardless of the list mode.
